prompt:
Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1436
Claimant:
Melody Pacheco
Adjuster:
Christopher Wong
11/16/2023
First notice of loss received from the claimant, who reports being stopped at a signal when a vehicle struck the rear of
the insured car. The claimant is not represented by counsel and has asked for a copy of the claim file once it is open.
11/25/2023
Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was active at the time of the collision. No issues
with the policy terms were found.
12/27/2023
Obtained the police report, which lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle at the scene. The responding
officer's notes match the claimant's description of the impact.
03/29/2024
Reviewed the photographs submitted by the claimant. They confirm the location of the damage and the general
position of both vehicles, though they do not show the moment of impact. No independent witnesses have come
forward.
04/11/2024
Inspected the vehicle. The rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail lgiht assembly damage is largely consistent with the
described impact speed and direction. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.
05/08/2024
Spoke with the claimant about reported neck and back strain. The claimant described the same account of the
collision as in the initial report, with the same sequence of events and details.
05/19/2024
Medical records show the clamiant was treated for the same body area within the last two years. The prior condition
appears to add to the current complaints, so the adjuster is noting it for the medical review.
06/03/2024
Revieewd the injury against the kind and force of the collision. The reported symptoms fit well with the type of impact
described and the damage to the vehicle.
06/25/2024
Treatment followed a typical course of care. Visits and therapy sessions have tapered off as the claimant reports
improvement in range of motion and pain levels.
06/27/2024
Checked for any indication that the damage predates the start of coverage. Nothing in the file suggests that it does,
and the policy effective dates fall well before the loss.
07/01/2024
Reviewed the file summary. Liability appears clear on the basis of the police report and vehicle damage, and the
claim is recommended to proceed to settlement review pending receipt of final treatment records.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
{"findings": [{"feature": "", "rating": "", "confidence": "", "quote": "", "reason": ""}]}
